newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX May power futures expire higher to meet cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX May power futures expire higher to meet cash.

text.p: NYMEX May electricity expired higher Friday to meet spot western cash prices which eased again on falling demand but still traded at a premium to futures.
May California-Oregon Border (COB) futures expired up 81 cents at $14.71 a megawatt hour (MWh) after posting a session high at $14.90.
June COB settled up 60 cents at $13.31 after hitting a high of $13.50. Other COB months ended up five to 20 cents.
May Palo Verde (PV) futures expired up 22 cents at $18.20, near the day's high at $18.20. June PV settled up six cents at $18.36. Deferred PV contracts ended two to 10 cents lower.
Firm, peak power prices for Monday at COB finished at $16.75-17.75, down from Thursday's $17.50-19.00, while those at PV ended at $17.00-18.00 down from $18.00-19.00 yesterday.

In addition to physical prices, May COB was boosted by Western Systems Coordinating Council board's approval to increase the spring transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie to 7,200 megawatt (MW) from the current 6,250 MW.
Market sources said potential of more power flowing to the Southwest was supportive for Northwest electricity prices.
"It's going to take energy from the Northwest into the Southwest," said an East Coast paper broker.
Near-term prospect for the Northwest market was also enhanced by limited daily surplus power offered by Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) in May, traders said.
"Hydro doesn't mean anything if BPA is not in the market," said a Houston futures trader.
Sources at the federal agency told Reuters today that BPA may not have surplus power to sell during peak demand hours next month due to prior block sales.

May PV prices are expected to receive support by news that Southern California Edison Co would extend the outage at the 1,080 MW San Onofre nuclear unit 3 to end-June from mid-June for structural repairs at the unit's steam generators, market sources said.
Forecasts called for Northwest temperatures to average above normal this weekend and into early next week, while in the Southwest, readings would moderate to near normal levels regionwide.
The northern and eastern sections of the Southwest would continue to see cloudy skies with showers and thunderstorms in the valleys and snow in the upper mountains through tomorrow.
NYMEX estimated 808 COB and 636 PV contracts were sold, up from yesterday's 767 COB and 463 PV lots.
